answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains structured like a trellis of verified interactions. Using zero-knowledge proofs, an agent proves unique lineage and computational work without leaking data, standing as a firm jetty against fraud. Registering clustered swarms triggers an exponential capital exhaustion fee that scales superlinearly ($O(2^n)$) per clone, facing a gale of prohibitive costs that renders mass Sybil deployment mathematically ruinous.
